To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) letter detection in the function words for and the is no more difficult when they appear in adjacent locations in the sentence (familiar sequence) than when they appear apart (less familiar) and (2)...

letter detection in function words is contingent on their syntactic roles within phrases, and that the syntactic role of a word is determined by its position relative to clause boundaries and the presence or absence of commas between clauses.

letter detection in very common function-word sequences is (1) not facilitated by the sequence appearing in an adjacent sentence location (familiarity effect) and (2), in the case of the sequence for, is facilitated when it appears in separate clauses (clause-separation effect).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the processing of function-word sequences is unitized.
the question whether the human visual system has the ability to detect and identify the individual letters in a word.
the nature of the cognitive processes that underlie reading comprehension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
letter detection is contingent upon syntactic structure.
syntactic structure is a powerful determinant of the ease with which letters are detected in adjacent function words.
the unitization of frequent function words is not the only factor that affects the detection of letters in adjacent function words, but that syntactic structure also has a strong effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
syntactic structure has an effect on letter detection in common phrases.
the effects of syntactic processing on letter detection are more pronounced in the case of adjacent function words.
the syntactic structures in a sentence can be processed in parallel, and the syntactic structures are processed before the semantic structures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
letter-level processing in very common function-word sequences is not unitary, but rather, it is sensitive to the syntactic structure in which the words appear.
syntactic structure can have a profound effect on letter detection in function words.
syntactic information can be extracted during reading and that this information is used by the reader to process the text.
